themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendors have exploded to 6 complaints this week compared to a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4,700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed operators or a coordinated enforcement crackdown worth investigating.
evidence: 6 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 17.76)
Signal is brand-new—no prior spike pattern in 90-day history
Geographic concentration: CD 301 (Greenpoint/Williamsburg) is food-vendor-dense neighborhood
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors flooding the neighborhood? Interview Department of Health & Mental Hygiene about enforcement activity this week.
Are legitimate vendors complaining about competition or enforcement? Talk to street food operators about what changed.

themes_detail.label: Park Rules & Animal Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, park-related violations have spiked sharply: 4 complaints about rule violations (967% above 8-week average of 0.4) and 29 animal-in-park complaints (293% above baseline of 7.4), suggesting either new park enforcement or a behavioral shift worth investigating.
evidence: 4 Violation of Park Rules complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
29 Animal in a Park complaints THIS WEEK vs 7.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.93)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously this week—suggests coordinated shift in park use or enforcement
reporting_angles: Did NYPD or Parks Dept launch a new enforcement initiative in Greenpoint/Williamsburg parks this week?
Are residents reporting loose dogs or off-leash violations at specific parks (e.g., McCarren Park, East River waterfront)?

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking & Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints have surged to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1,500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—occurring simultaneously with park-rule and animal violations, suggesting a potential disorder or enforcement pattern emerging in a specific park or waterfront area.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)
Spike is concurrent with park violations and animal complaints—suggests geographic/temporal clustering
No prior spike pattern in 90-day baseline
reporting_angles: Interview residents in neighborhoods near waterfront parks (McCarren, East River Waterfront) about daytime disorder.
Contact NYPD 94th Precinct about whether they've increased patrols or incident reports this week.

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Crisis (2 Weeks Ago)
themes_detail.summary: Two weeks ago, dirty condition complaints spiked to 107 versus a baseline of 35.8 per week (199% increase, z-score: 6.55), and illegal dumping surged to 39 complaints versus 14.6 baseline (167% increase, z-score: 6.19), indicating a significant but resolved sanitation episode—worth checking if it has recurred.
evidence: 107 dirty condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs 35.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.55)
39 illegal dumping complaints 2 weeks ago vs 14.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.19)
Both spikes occurred in same week—suggests single triggering event (e.g., sanitation strike, equipment failure, or construction)
reporting_angles: Was there a sanitation disruption 2 weeks ago? Check with NYC Sanitation (DSNY) about truck breakdowns, labor actions, or service interruptions.
Has the district returned to normal cleanup levels, or are cleanup problems ongoing? Compare current complaint volume to baseline.

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise & Fireworks (3 Weeks Ago)
themes_detail.summary: Three weeks ago, illegal fireworks complaints reached 12 (1,500% above baseline of 0.8, z-score: 6.86) and vehicle noise hit 45 (219% above baseline of 14.1, z-score: 6.04)—a past spike that has likely subsided but warrants monitoring for recurrence or pattern.
evidence: 12 illegal fireworks complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.86)
45 vehicle noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs 14.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.04)
Both spikes are now 3 weeks old; currently less urgent unless new spike materializes
reporting_angles: Was there a specific event (concert, holiday, street racing event) 3 weeks ago that triggered both spikes?
Monitor for recurrence as weather warms or event calendar approaches similar dates.
